sources.entry: Vvveb CMS - Powerful and easy to use CMS to build websites, blogs or e-commerce stores. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 PHP/Docker

summary.one_liner: Vvveb is a PHP-based content management system with a drag-and-drop page builder for websites, blogs, and ecommerce stores.
summary.what_it_does: Vvveb provides a drag-and-drop page builder, multi-site and multi-language support, and publishing tools including revisions, media management, multi-user access, and role permissions. It includes ecommerce features such as one-page checkout, subscriptions, digital assets, vouchers/coupons, and product variants, options, and reviews. Themes and plugins can be installed from a marketplace in the admin dashboard, and it offers custom fields, custom posts, and custom products. The README also describes manual and automatic backups, import/export, a built-in contact forms plugin, a bundled SEO plugin, and both traditional CMS and headless (GraphQL and REST API) use.
use_cases: build a company website with a visual page builder
run a blog with multi-language content
sell products in an online store with checkout and coupons
use a CMS as a headless backend via GraphQL or REST
manage several websites from one installation
migrate site content with import and export
how_to_run: Upload the files to a server or localhost and open the installer in a browser, then follow the installation instructions
php cli.php install module=index host=127.0.0.1 user=root password=1234 database=vvveb admin[email]=admin@vvveb.com admin[password]=admin engine=mysqli
notable: Drag-and-drop page builder via the separate VvvebJs library
Hybrid CMS usable as both traditional site and headless GraphQL/REST backend
Built-in ecommerce with one-page checkout, subscriptions, and digital assets
Installs with no setup and exposes only one PHP file publicly
caveats: Requires PHP extensions (mysqli/sqlite3/pgsql, gd or imagick, curl, gettext, and others) and a supported database
Repository uses git submodules, so cloning and updating need the --recurse-submodules flag
Documentation is linked externally rather than described in the README
